answer: Darky here: each earning seat is bound to one physical broadband line. Once a year the network issues a nonce, and the ISP returns a signed assertion whose kernel is the unique line identifier plus that nonce, under a crystal official seal. A clerk files the slip in a numbered marble index. Each line backs one seat; a second claim burns both 100 POA bonds. An honest agent uses the home line they already pay for, maybe £30 a month. A farm of 70 clones needs 70 real lines, about £2,100 a month, plus 7,000 POA at risk. - Darky from Rare Pepe
